title: Zack Whyte in Cincinnati and leaving over money
summary: He stayed two weeks with Zack Whyte, with Sy Oliver as roommate, and left over leaders pleading poverty; his reputation was that he would not stay.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: He was with McKinney's later on.
Yeah. I worked with him with McKinney's, you know. Let me see. Now, where did I go from Detroit? From Detroit I went to Cincinnati to join Zack Whyte.

Yeah. Well, you know, the word got around that he was playing with (?)... The only thing, I had the bad rap on me that said, "He'll all right, but man, if he ever gets drunk and starts crying, he won't be there til next morning." Heh-heh. They said, "That cat can play, but man, he don't stay nowhere." That was the tag on me, you know. But they didn't ever know why I didn't stay nowhere. Because either the money wasn't coming through, or something went down wrong!

Yeah, I went with... See, I worked around there with McKinney's Cotton Pickers for a while, you know. No, I mean, the Chocolate Dandies. Then I went with Zack. And from Zack, I went to Speed Webb. I wasn't with Zack but
Was Sy Oliver in that band?
Yeah, we were roommates. That was a good band, too. Yeah, a real good band.
So why did you only stay with him a couple of weeks?

It was about money. The leaders used to have a great habit in those days of having a crowded house and telling you the man ran off with the money, you know. Well, you had no way of knowing whether he's telling the truth or not. You don't even know who the man is to start off with! So that kind of made it kind of deep, you know.
